rules.rule: The page (web/) is type-checked like the server, with svelte-check
rules.why: npm run check only covered src/; 13 errors had piled up in the page, some hiding real mistakes. svelte-check is a local dev dependency on TypeScript 6 (7 sits beside it as @typescript/native for the server check). Through npx it brought its own svelte and reported false errors; its --tsgo mode passed a planted error

rules.rule: Nullable state is typed with the generic: $state<T | null>(null)
rules.why: let x: T | null = $state(null) makes TypeScript narrow x to never, so every use of it goes unchecked

rules.rule: web/ and src/ never import each other; shapes they share go in web/src/lib/types.ts
rules.why: the page is bundled for the browser and the server runs on node: code crossing over breaks one of them

rules.rule: The GTK desktop window builds with every change to it
rules.why: it is Rust beside a TypeScript project: nothing else would notice it broke

rules.rule: No setTimeout or requestAnimationFrame to fix an ordering problem in a component: find what it waits for
rules.why: timers patch over a missing dependency, then get copied as the pattern; they also make the page janky

rules.rule: What cockpit keeps for a project stays in its .cockpit/ or in cockpit's own state folder, never in the project's setup
rules.why: cockpit is used on work projects whose structure isn't ours to change

rules.rule: Colours, corners and shadows come from the tokens in web/src/app.css :root (var(--r-m), var(--shadow-pop), var(--accent)…), never raw values
rules.why: the page had drifted to 10 corner radii and 12 shadows; one-off values make panels look subtly unrelated

rules.rule: Build controls from web/src/components/ui/ (IconButton, Menu) before writing new button or popover CSS; add a piece there when a pattern repeats
rules.why: every panel had grown its own popover and button styles

rules.rule: One main action per toolbar; settings you rarely change go in a Menu, not on a toolbar. Repeated actions are icon buttons, text buttons are for dialogs
rules.why: the chat toolbar gave the model switch (almost never changed) as much room as the conversation title

rules.rule: No confirm(), alert() or prompt(): a destructive action asks in place (the button turns into a red "Revert" that a second click confirms, leaving cancels)
rules.why: the browser's dialog is huge, blocks the whole window and looks foreign; three older ones remain (unsaved files on switching project or closing a tab)
